disclaimer: Reminder reference only — NOT legal authority. Season dates, zones, and limits are set annually and can change. Always verify current regulations with the Arizona Game and Fish Department before trapping.

license_summary.method_warning: Under A.R.S. section 17-301(D), leghold traps, instant-kill body-gripping traps, poison, and snares are prohibited on public land, subject to statutory exceptions (e.g., licensed private-land trapping with landowner permission). Check the official trapping regulations for the current exceptions.
license_summary.trapping_license: An Arizona trapping license is required to trap furbearers. Consult the AZGFD trapping regulations for license types, fees, trap registration, and check requirements.

verification.confirmation_notes: The 2026–27 Arizona Trapping Regulations (Commission Order 23) were downloaded from AZGFD's official regulations page and verified 2026-09-18: November 1, 2026 – February 28, 2027 for both species groups, with the beaver/muskrat Unit 34B exclusion and the bobcat tag/jaw/CITES requirements. The proclamation lists 'foxes,' 'skunks,' and 'weasels' generically — modeled without inventing species-level seasons. Closed entries (Mexican gray wolf, jaguar, ocelot, black-footed ferret) reflect federal ESA endangered status; AZGFD confirms only specifically authorized species may be hunted/trapped and lists these as endangered.
known_gaps: Scientific names are standard taxonomy, NOT stated in Commission Order 23 — all flagged scientific_name_verified=false; foxes, skunks, and weasels are null because the proclamation is generic.
The proclamation does not enumerate protected wildlife; closed entries were added from federal ESA listings rather than an AZGFD trapping-pamphlet list.
Excluded units (NWRs, Mohave County Park Lands, Units 11M, 25M, 26M, 38M, 34B) are modeled descriptively — the app cannot resolve unit boundaries.
Bobcat CITES-sealing details (locations/deadline) are summarized; users must check the proclamation.
